report.title: Checkout API latency and errors due to connection pool contention
report.summary: Checkout API is experiencing increased latency and errors. Evidence points to a recent change reducing the inventory client connection pool maximum, leading to contention. A mitigation has been proposed to revert this change.

findings.text: Checkout API p95 latency increased from 420ms to 2840ms and the API error rate rose from 0.3% to 6.8% from 14:15 UTC.
One representative trace recorded HTTP 504 and shows significant time (2190ms) spent waiting to acquire a database connection during an inventory.reserve call.
Eighteen of twenty sampled slow traces exhibit database connection pool waits exceeding 1800ms.
The checkout release 8f2c1d, at 14:12 UTC, reduced the inventory client connection pool maximum from 20 to 5.

nextSteps: Await approval from the Checkout Experience team for the proposed mitigation.
Monitor checkout-api metrics closely after mitigation to confirm latency and error rate return to baseline.
Compare inventory-api connection pool metrics against baseline to validate the effect of the change.
report.uncertainty: While temporal correlation is strong and supported by trace data, all sampled traces may not represent all requests. The absence of specific child spans in some areas limits the scope of inference.
report.customerUpdate: We are investigating an issue affecting some checkout processes, leading to delays. Our teams are actively working to resolve this. We will provide another update as soon as more information is available.

proposal.action: Revert the inventory client connection pool maximum from 5 to 20.
proposal.rationale: The connection pool maximum was reduced from 20 to 5 at 14:12 UTC (E3), correlating with the start of increased latency and errors in checkout-api (E1). Traces show significant time spent waiting for database connections (E2), and pool pending requests increased (E4). This evidence is consistent with connection pool contention.
proposal.expectedEffect: This action is expected to alleviate connection pool contention, thereby reducing checkout-api latency and error rates to baseline levels.

Samples do not prove all requests behave the same way.

retrievedEvidence.title: Database CPU and payment time stayed stable
retrievedEvidence.detail: Database CPU is 36%, baseline 34%. Payment authorization p95 is 140ms, baseline 135ms. Pool pending requests rose from 0 to 84. These observations favor pool contention over a payment-provider slowdown or database CPU saturation.

report.title: Inventory-to-Database Network Path Connection Issues Impacting Checkout API
report.summary: Checkout API is experiencing increased latency and errors, consistent with connection rejection issues on the inventory-to-database network path. A recent firewall policy update correlates with the onset of these issues.

findings.text: Checkout API p95 latency and error rate rose at 17:14 UTC, degrading user experience across all release cohorts.
Sampled flow records show 18% rejected connections on the inventory subnet to inventory-db port 5432 after 17:14 UTC, significantly above baseline.
A representative slow trace and sampled slow traces indicate substantial delays (up to 2450ms) in the observed payment-path delay to inventory-db.
A firewall policy update for the inventory-to-database path occurred at 17:11 UTC, shortly before the degradation was observed.

nextSteps: Network Platform should validate the impact of the 17:11 UTC firewall policy update on inventory-to-database connection attempts.
Inventory Services should review their connection pooling and retry mechanisms for handling connection failures to the database.
Infrastructure Operations should collect per-device packet captures on the inventory-to-database network path to confirm connection rejections.
report.uncertainty: Correlation between the firewall policy update and observed connection issues is strong, but direct causal linkage for fleet-wide impact requires further validation. No physical infrastructure issues have been confirmed.
report.customerUpdate: We are investigating an issue affecting transaction processing, leading to increased latency and errors. Our teams are actively working to identify and resolve the underlying cause. We will provide updates as more information becomes available.

Successful database queries and payment calls remain near baseline.
